## Requirements: Mobile terminal density and symmetric usable insets

### Context / owner request (2026-10-29)

After review of #2581, the owner reported two visible App/mobile terminal problems: **rows still feel too far apart**, and **the Terminal has visibly unequal left/right whitespace**. **Follow-up owner decision (2026-10-29):** some balanced blank space on both sides is intentional and visually desirable; columns remain fixed and the font size must fit the full grid **within the actual remaining width, without horizontal scrolling**. This supersedes this Issue's earlier proposed overflow/scroll policy; do not implement a scrolling fallback as the product design. **Latest owner decision (2026-10-29): mobile has NO Nession-imposed minimum font size. The font size must be calculated from each screen's available content width and the Session's fixed column count. The existing 6px mobile fit floor must be removed, not treated as a product/readability constraint.**

This is a **new Product/Experience layout decision**, not an incomplete #2581 engine architecture SC or a recurrence of #1092's old fixture FitAddon bug. #2581 has completed its engine/component refactor and was closed; do not reopen it or change its acceptance history. Related: #1092 (older, different fixture overflow cause), #1081 (App edge gestures), #2487 / #2557 (fixed Session cols and 96 default), #1503 (capsule scroll/resize), #2581 (engine boundary).

#### Source-level baseline (main, 2026-10-29)

- `design/tokens/experience/app.json` / generated `design/generated/terminal.ts`: App `fontSize: 11.5px` maximum, **xterm `lineHeight: 1.31`**, `padX: 14px`, `padY: 14px`. Web counterpart uses `lineHeight: 1.19`, `padX: 18px`. The App 1.31 was intentionally converted from an older mockup (`11.5px × CSS 1.7 = 19.55px`), **not a current device-verified optimal value**. `lineHeight` is multiplied by xterm's measured font box, not by CSS `font-size`.
- `web/src/product/terminal/components/TerminalViewport.tsx` uses symmetric outer `padding-inline: var(--nession-terminal-pad-x)`; this fact alone does **not** guarantee the painted grid is centered.
- `web/src/index.css` lines around 200–213 explicitly use `.xterm { max-width: var(--nession-local-terminal-content-width); margin-inline: 0; }` on App/narrow widths, enabling `margin-inline: auto` only at **≥1024px**. When `cols × measured cell width < content box width`, spare width accumulates on the **right**.
- `web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/view/TerminalGeometry.ts` fits the actual measured cell to an Agent/Session-authored **fixed column count** and publishes `--nession-local-terminal-content-width` and `data-terminal-cols-fit`; no automatic mobile column reduction is allowed.
- #2557 selected **96 columns** as release default. Existing `sizing.ts` hardcodes `MIN_TERMINAL_FIT_FONT_SIZE = 6` and passes that minimum through `fitFontToColumns`; `TerminalGeometry` limits mobile `maxFontSize` through `PROFILES.mobile.fontSize` (currently 11.5px). **These are existing implementation limits, not mobile product requirements.** On a 375px phone with 14px insets on each side, the content box is ~347px; at 96 cols the average rendered cell budget is ~3.615px. **Do not assume 6px always overflows:** an earlier fixture/prototype observed ~4px cells at 6px, while the 2026-10-29 Chromium 144 source-formula probe with JetBrains Mono Regular gave ~3.333 CSS px per Canvas/WebGL cell at DPR 3, fitting 96 columns in ~320px (not an actual mounted xterm validation). The existing 6px lower clamp still must be eliminated for App under the owner's latest decision. Compute the best fitting font from real measured cells, including smaller-than-6px values when needed. The old 11.5px App profile must not freeze mobile font sizing where more width is available; it may initialize measurement but final App fit derives from width and cols.
- `web/src/app/experiences/app/edgeBand.ts` and `workSurface.ts` grant the shell directional gestures in a 28px band at each shell edge (#1081). The former left-align policy cites gesture reach. Any centering decision must preserve those gestures and terminal selection/mouse/IME.
- `web/src/app/fixture/FixtureTerminal.tsx` uses the same App profile and emulator but runs its own layout fit; fixture and actual attached-session behavior must both be checked.

**Verification status:** CSS/token/geometry causal paths confirmed statically; user observation confirms the visible symptom. The 6px/96-cols/375px arithmetic is grounded in the earlier measured prototype/issue, but **live xterm in the current main build and native-device pixel evidence are still Pending**. A final implementation must prove no-scroll fitting at representative device widths. If the browser/xterm engine has a **proven intrinsic rendering or font-size precision limit** that prevents the full fixed grid fitting a tested supported device, document the exact renderer behavior and keep acceptance Pending until a compatible rendering implementation is found. Do not invent another product minimum font size, or quietly introduce overflow, clipping, scaling, or per-device column changes.

### xterm.js minimum font research (2026-10-29; upstream source + browser metric probe)

- **Exact Nession lockfile versions:** `@xterm/xterm 5.5.0`, `@xterm/addon-canvas 0.7.0`, `@xterm/addon-webgl 0.19.0`. The repository's `web/package.json` uses caret ranges, so verify these resolved versions rather than relying on package ranges alone.
- **No `fontSize` numeric lower bound in the xterm.js 5.5.0 option validator.** [`OptionsService.ts` at 5.5.0](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/5.5.0/src/common/services/OptionsService.ts#L148-L200) imposes minima on `lineHeight`, `tabStopWidth`, etc., but not on `fontSize`. This supports removing Nession's artificial 6px floor.
- **Measured font-cell width must remain positive.** [`CharSizeService.ts` at 5.5.0](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/5.5.0/src/browser/services/CharSizeService.ts#L61-L127) uses OffscreenCanvas `measureText('W')` / DOM fallback and retains only valid positive width **and** height. CSS `fontSize` being accepted does not prove a functional terminal.
- **Device-pixel quantization is the actual technical boundary.** [`CanvasRenderer.ts` at 5.5.0](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/5.5.0/addons/addon-canvas/src/CanvasRenderer.ts#L157-L176) and [`WebglRenderer.ts` at 5.5.0](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/5.5.0/addons/addon-webgl/src/WebglRenderer.ts#L534-L583) use `Math.floor(measuredCharWidth × devicePixelRatio)`; a font producing **less than 1 device pixel** per cell can yield **zero device-cell width**, so the renderer is no longer a valid terminal grid even if `fontSize` was accepted. Upstream [#6015](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/6015) also documents canvas/WebGL vs DOM fractional-width differences.
- **Browser metric probe (not full xterm runtime):** Headless Chromium **144**, local *JetBrains Mono Regular OTF* (the Nession face is *JetBrains Mono Variable*, so not identical), viewport **375 CSS px**, padding **14px/side**, `cols=96`, available **347px**. Per `CharSizeService`-style OffscreenCanvas measurements and 5.5.0 Canvas/WebGL formula: at **DPR 3**, font 7px → 96×4=**384px** (does not fit), 6.5px → 96×(11/3)=**352px** (does not fit), **6px → 96×(10/3)=320px** (fits geometric grid), **5px → 96×3=288px** (fits), **1px → 96×(1/3)=32px** (nonzero but clearly tiny). At **DPR 1**, 1px yields **zero** rounded device-cell width. DPR alone can change the threshold and glyph-grid slack by whole device pixels.
- **Qualifying observations:** These figures verify the browser font metrics and the **specific upstream dimension formulas** in a live Chromium browser; they **do not** establish whether the entire terminal buffer, rasterized glyphs, cursor, Chinese text, IME, TUI or native iOS Safari renders correctly. They do not prove that 6px universally fits or that arbitrarily small font sizes can be rendered. Renderer floor/quantization can produce overlap even when `cols × cellWidth <= availableWidth`.
- **Engineering consequence:** Maintain **no Nession-defined minimum font size**, yet reject nonpositive/invalid measured cell dimensions as an **intrinsic renderer constraint**, and do not pass acceptance by counting a zero-width grid as fitting. Verify small-font full xterm DOM/Canvas/WebGL screenshot output, glyph/cell/hit-target alignment and real iPhone DPR/zoom, with complete first/last column visibility. No silent horizontal scroll, column change or clip.

**Evidence status:** Upstream source **verified**, independent Chromium metric reproduction **verified**, full xterm 5.5.0 rendering and native iOS Safari **Pending**. No repository code modified by this research; acceptance SCs remain Pending.

### Product decision to implement

**Horizontal presentation model (approved):** For a supported App viewport, let `W` be the actual screen/terminal viewport content width, `P` the deliberate symmetric horizontal inset, and `C` the Agent/Session-authoritative fixed columns (96 for a new default Session). Compute `W_available = W - 2 × P`. Select the **best-fitting App font size dynamically from `W_available` and `C`**, using the live xterm renderer's measured cell width `cellWidth(fontSize)`. The chosen size is the largest visually suitable font whose actual grid fits: `C × cellWidth(fontSize) <= W_available`. Center the painted grid within the remaining content box; allow tasteful symmetric blank space.

**No application-level minimum font size on mobile.** Do not clamp the computed App result to 6px, 8px, or any replacement fixed threshold. Remove the mobile path's use of `MIN_TERMINAL_FIT_FONT_SIZE` in `sizing.ts`, `TerminalGeometry.ts` and `FixtureTerminal.tsx`; keep desktop/manual zoom policy separate. The current 11.5px `PROFILES.mobile.fontSize` must not prevent the App from recomputing a suitable font from the screen and cols: it may be a starting probe/default until a renderer measurement exists, **not an unconditional fixed output or mobile fit ceiling**.

1. **Compact App-only leading.** Compare the current xterm line-height **1.31** with tighter 1.10/1.14/1.18 candidates and select an App token using real glyph, CJK, cursor, TUI and IME evidence. Do not alter Web line-height.
2. **Responsive dynamic mobile font fit.** Recompute when the usable screen/container width, horizontal inset, fixed Session cols, orientation, font face or renderer metrics change. Width/cols define the fit, not a device-class fixed font. Probe actual cell measurements with suitable convergence/precision rather than assuming linear `fontSize × 0.6`; tolerate fractional values and rounding/quantization, verify the final size against the actual painted grid. A height-only change updates rows without gratuitously re-fitting width. No hardcoded mobile font-size floor.
3. **Balanced intentional horizontal whitespace.** Preserve symmetric App `padX` (currently 14px each side) or adjust only its design token with evidence. Center the whole measured fixed grid within the inner content box and share any residual space evenly. No CSS transform/zoom to fake fitting or second set of device columns.
4. **All columns visible, no horizontal scrolling.** For supported App widths including 375/390/393/430/440 CSS px, require the painted first and last columns visible simultaneously, `data-terminal-cols-fit=true`, and no horizontal xterm scrolling/clipping. **The old `fits=false → overflow-x: auto` fallback is superseded as a Product behavior.** Do not replace it with `overflow-x:hidden` clipping. If a specific xterm/browser renderer cannot measure/draw a small enough cell for this contract, record and reproduce the **intrinsic renderer limitation**, keep SC-03 Pending, and investigate the rendering boundary; do not restore any Nession-imposed font floor.
5. **Keep App edge gestures and PTY semantics.** The centered grid and intentional whitespace must not steal either 28px shell gesture band (#1081) or change terminal selection, TUI mouse/paste, IME, focus or cell-hit mapping. Mobile requires no horizontal terminal scroll gesture.
6. **One source and fixture parity.** Update `TerminalGeometry`, `sizing.ts`, and `FixtureTerminal` to share a consistent **unbounded-below mobile fitting policy** based on actual metrics. Update App design token source and regenerate artifacts if leading or App default/initial metrics change; do not directly edit `design/generated/terminal.ts`. Amend narrow-width left-alignment and overflow-fallback prose in `docs/design/terminal/terminal-sizing.md` and related Terminal Surface specs. Keep 96 default and live Agent/Session-authoritative columns, and preserve SessionRuntime/ControlLease, ordered output, tmux/PTY and P2P/Relay behavior.

**Rendering reality:** “No minimum font size” means no **application-imposed threshold**. It does not assert that arbitrarily small CSS font values or fractional cells are supported by every current xterm renderer/browser. Such a real renderer limit is a testable implementation blocker to solve at the rendering boundary, not permission to change this product contract or fabricate a passing fit.

### Measurement and reproduction plan

Test the real xterm App implementation (not only a mocked simulator) at **375/390/393/430/440 CSS px**, portrait/landscape, loaded/loading webfont, DPR variation, resting/open capsule and soft keyboard. Include 96-column Sessions and existing Sessions with other Agent-authoritative widths.

Capture: viewport/content-box width and both padding values; actual `cols`; selected `fontSize` including candidates **below 6px** when needed; measured `cellWidth`/`cellHeight`; `cols × cellWidth <= contentWidth`; `data-terminal-cols-fit`; painted grid bounds; first/last column visibility; symmetric left/right gutter difference; `scrollWidth/clientWidth/scrollLeft`; glyph/cursor/CJK/box-drawing/TUI behavior; shell edge gesture and IME/selection mapping.

For each width, test at least two known-configured Session column values and verify that narrowing the viewport **reduces the chosen font size rather than reducing cols, clipping or revealing a horizontal scrollbar**. Show that no `MIN_TERMINAL_FIT_FONT_SIZE` or equivalent lower-bound clamp executes on the App path, that further shrinkage is allowed as required by measured cells, and that the selected font uses the available content width effectively without excessive slack.

Use Playwright browser measurements and actual xterm metrics; if native iOS Safari/manual capture is unavailable, distinguish Pending device-specific evidence from proven browser behavior. If cell quantization, xterm option validation, browser rasterization or layout precision means a supported width cannot fit all fixed columns, produce a deterministic reproduction and keep the affected SC Pending while repairing the renderer compatibility problem. Do **not** silently accept a fallback minimum size, change the logical columns, or disguise a crop as fit.

### Prototype

- Decision: Not needed — this adjusts existing leading and an already-defined fixed-column fit/alignment pattern, not a new interaction paradigm. The real-xterm App fixture plus measured before/after screenshots are higher fidelity than a mockup.
- **Scenario:** 375/390/430px App → compare old/new line height and balanced gutters → measure 96-column full-grid fit without horizontal scrolling → edge swipe and TUI gestures → restore Session/rotate.
- **Status:** Not needed.
- **Artifact:** Existing #2487 interactive sizing lab may inform constraints, but **does not count as live-renderer acceptance**.

### Verification tier

**Proposed `verification:integration` (L2).** One experience token/layout change crosses renderer font measurement, Session fixed cols and App gesture ownership. Use narrow source-aligned browser/fixture cases, not blanket Full E2E. PR-head is the earliest safe stage for design source and deterministic browser evidence; if a native device cannot be accessed, mark native-specific observations Pending, not Pass.

### Knowledge Impact

- Decision: Read
- Related knowledge: `Web terminal emulator engine and component ownership` (published from #2581); canonical `docs/design/terminal/terminal-sizing.md`, `docs/design/design-system/patterns/terminal-surface.md`, `design/tokens/experience/app.json`, #2487, #2557.
- Reason: A localized App visual-density and **unbounded-below measured font fitting** policy refinement belongs in its current canonical design token + Terminal Surface docs, rather than creating a duplicate general architecture article.
- Owner and timing: Web/App Terminal design owner reviews the existing terminal knowledge entry during implementation; if the change invalidates durable knowledge assertions, reconcile via the governed knowledge-branch flow before acceptance; otherwise document why no publication is required.
- Evidence: Exact-sha token source/compiled output, browser geometry/gesture receipts and canonical design-doc diff.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 Real App emulator's selected line-height produces a visibly and measurably more compact row than the existing 1.31 baseline without glyph/cursor/box-drawing/IME clipping at representative widths and fit font sizes, while Web leading remains unchanged.
- [ ] SC-02 At 375/390/393/430/440px and supported orientations with a 96-column Session, the complete painted grid is centered within deliberate symmetric horizontal insets: total left/right gutter difference is at most 1 CSS px (allowing renderer rounding), and the first and final columns are both visible.
- [ ] SC-03 The mobile font-fit path has **no Nession-defined minimum font-size clamp** (in `sizing.ts`, Geometry, fixture or a replacement helper); the chosen font is recalculated from current usable screen width and authoritative fixed cols using actual xterm cell measurements, including **below 6px whenever needed**. The measured result satisfies `cols × cellWidth <= contentWidth`, `data-terminal-cols-fit=true` and **no horizontal scrolling or clipping** at all tested supported widths; engine-intrinsic unsupported measurements are reported as Pending, not misrepresented as success.
- [ ] SC-04 App shell's 28px directional edge navigation works from both edges; xterm selection, TUI mouse/wheel, vertical touch scroll, IME/focus and tap-to-cell remain correct after font recomputation and centering.
- [ ] SC-05 Orientation, width, font load, capsule/keyboard geometry, existing Session attach, takeover and reconnect preserve the Agent's authoritative columns; narrower width changes font rather than columns, height-only changes rows without unnecessary font re-fit or redundant remote SIGWINCH.
- [ ] SC-06 Fixture and live terminal use the same measured unbounded-below mobile fit, symmetric insets and no-horizontal-scroll presentation, with exact-SHA browser geometry/visual evidence; App Experience token sources/generated artifacts and canonical docs reflect the approved policy without unrelated Web metric changes.

## E2E Verification

### New
- none: extend existing real-xterm App/Terminal browser suites with symmetric-gutter, compact leading, **font-fit below 6px (no application floor)**, full 96-column no-scroll fit and edge-gesture cases instead of another overlapping spec family.

## Product alignment

- [x] **VISION.md:** makes the cross-device terminal easier to read without moving complexity to the user.
- [x] **PRINCIPLE.md:** layout precision and visual hierarchy, not decorative additional chrome; retain work-surface/gesture ownership.
- [x] **Canonical docs reviewed:** Terminal Surface, terminal sizing, Web layering, #1081, #2487, #2557, #2581.
- [x] **Deviation explicit:** revises the older App 1.31 leading, narrow-width left alignment, **all application-imposed mobile font minimums**, and the previous horizontal-overflow fallback. No change to fixed Session columns, authoritative ControlLease or ordered stream/ACK invariants. A proven xterm/browser intrinsic limitation requires a renderer fix/evidence, not a hidden minimum.

---
**Status:** Draft — owner explicitly requires **no minimum mobile font size**, measured responsive font size based on real screen/content width and fixed Session cols, balanced whitespace and **no horizontal scrolling**. Implementation and exact-device/browser acceptance remain Pending.
